'''Ronald Lewis Phillips''' (1940 – 25 August 2023)<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Kaeppler | first1=Shawn M. | last2=Springer | first2=Nathan | title=Remembering Ronald L. Phillips: Pioneer in crop biotechnology, mentor, and humanitarian | journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences | date=2024 | volume=121 | issue=5 | article-number=e2320943121 | doi=10.1073/pnas.2320943121 | doi-access=free | bibcode=2024PNAS..12120943K }}</ref> was an American [[biologist]] and a regents professor at the [[University of Minnesota]].<ref>{{cite journal|author=Phillips, R. L.|doi=10.1098/rsbm.2013.0012|doi-access=free|title=Norman Ernest Borlaug. 25 March 1914 -- 12 September 2009|journal=[[Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society]]|year=2013|volume=59|pages=59–72|s2cid=75211546}}</ref> In 1985 he was elected a fellow and the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aaas.org/fellows/historic|title = Historic Fellows &#124; American Association for the Advancement of Science}}</ref> and in 1991 he was elected to the [[National Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/ronald-l-phillips-ra75hz/|title=Ronald L. Phillips}}</ref>

==Education and career==
Phillips completed his B.S. and M.S. degrees from [[Purdue University]]. After completing his master's degree, moved to the University of Minnesota where he studied maize [[cytogenetics]] advised by [[Charles Burnham (geneticist)|Charles Burnham]],<ref>{{cite book |editor1=Peter A. Peterson |editor2=Angelo Bianchi |title=Maize genetics and breeding in the 20th century |date=1999 |publisher=World Scientific |location=Singapore |isbn=978-9810228668 |page=27}}</ref> graduating in 1966. After completing his PhD, he spent a short time as a postdoc at [[Cornell University]]. Since 1967, he has been a professor at the University of Minnesota. Officially retiring in 2010, he is now Regents Professor Emeritus at the University of Minnesota.<ref name=um>{{cite web |author1=<!-- -->|url=https://agronomy.cfans.umn.edu/department-directory/ronald-l-phillips|title=Ronald L. Phillips|work=<!----> |publisher=University of Minnesota, Department of Agronomy and Plant Genetics |date=25 June 2015 |access-date=October 7, 2019}}</ref>

==Research==
Ronald L. Phillips was the first to generate whole corn plants from cells grown in culture, which laid the foundation for, and sparked, a new industry, using cell-culture methods to genetically modify corn plants and other cereals. The corn cell line which is most widely used for genetic modification of corn has greatly accelerated the improvement of corn, as food, feed and fuel.<ref name=um/>

His research program at the University of Minnesota was one of the early programs in modern plant biotechnology related to agriculture. Research in the Phillips laboratory have further led to the identification of cells and plants with increased levels of essential amino acids and the development of an efficient DNA sequence mapping system used by plant scientists in genomics research.<ref name=um/>

He found was possible to introgress individual maize chromosomes into oat, where they were stably inherited. His lab generated a set nine oat lines each carrying the complete oat genome plus one maize chromosome<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Kynast | first1=Ralf G. | last2=Okagaki | first2=Ron J. | last3=Galatowitsch | first3=Mark W. | last4=Granath | first4=Shannon R. | last5=Jacobs | first5=Morrison S. | last6=Stec | first6=Adrian O. | last7=Rines | first7=Howard W. | last8=Phillips | first8=Ronald L. | title=Dissecting the maize genome by using chromosome addition and radiation hybrid lines | journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences | date=2004 | volume=101 | issue=26 | pages=9921–9926 | doi=10.1073/pnas.0403421101 | doi-access=free | pmid=15197265 | pmc=470774 }}</ref>

== Recognition ==
In 2006/7, he was awarded the [[Wolf Prize in Agriculture]] along with [[Michel A. J. Georges]] of the [[University of Liège]] "for groundbreaking discoveries in genetics and genomics, laying the foundations for improvements in crop and livestock breeding, and sparking important advances in plant and animal sciences".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.jewishvirtuallibrary.org/wolf-prize-recipients-in-agriculture|title=Wolf Prize Recipients in Agriculture|website=[[Jewish Virtual Library]]|access-date=October 7, 2019}}</ref>

In 2010 Phillips received the ISA Medal for Science from the [[University of Bologna]] and the Siehl Prize from the University of Minnesota.<ref name=um/>
